title: Along the Terraced Steps
story:
James descended from the high overlook, his hands finding purchase on the cool, moss-cushioned stone of the ancient agricultural terraces. The air here was markedly warmer than the windswept pass above, thick with the comforting scent of wet soil, wild marigolds, and towering stalks of green maize. Stepped down the mountainside in colossal emerald tiers, the fields caught the highland rain in tidy stone canals that gurgled with fresh mountain runoff.

Farther down the slope, the quiet mist gave way to the pulse of life in the valley basin. He listened to the heavy drops drumming against the broad corn leaves. He listened to the distant, celebratory pops of firecrackers echoing from a hamlet nestled in the valley below. He listened to the soft, familiar clink of the brass canister and compass swaying against his chest. Even far from home, the mountain moved to a steady, deliberate rhythm.

James slipped beneath the dry overhanging thatch of a roadside field shelter to shake the rain from his fur. Across the muddy stone path, festive blue-and-white paper banners hung strung between two carved wooden poles, fluttering vigorously in the highland breeze. He pulled out Barnaby's pocket compass and held it flat in his palm. The delicate dark needle shivered, spun, and settled resolutely toward the southern horizon, where the valley opened into rolling foothills and scattered settlements far beyond Oakhaven's reach.

Touching the colorful woven threads bound tight to his strap, James felt the lingering warmth of the memories he carried. The cozy rafters of the Archive Nook and the ticking of the great clock tower belonged to yesterday; his path now lay down through the green terraces and whatever lay waiting in the wide valley ahead. As the late afternoon mist softened into lavender shadows, James rested by the flowing water, watching the rain weave silver ripples into the ditch.
